Participle of the causative (‘made to fall’), agreeing with बलम् as the object of दृष्ट्वा: ‘seeing the army felled’.

mantras.anvaya: क्षणेन असुराणां तत् सर्वं बलं निपातितं दृष्ट्वा चण्डः ताम् अतिभीषणां कालीम् अभिदुद्राव।
mantras.anvaya_en: The first line is the object of दृष्ट्वा (‘seeing the army felled’); the main clause is चण्डः … कालीम् अभिदुद्राव.
mantras.lit: Having seen that whole army of the asuras laid low in a moment, Caṇḍa rushed at that exceedingly terrifying Kālī.
mantras.tr: When Caṇḍa saw the whole asura army laid low in a moment, he rushed at Kālī, terrible as she was.

comm.t: The army is gone, and the first general attacks. The opening half-line repeats 6.19 (क्षणेन तद्बलं सर्वम्), where the lion destroyed Dhūmralocana’s army in a moment: the text marks each rout with the same words.

Before k (here kṣ) the visarga stays visarga.
a + a → ā; the final m becomes anusvāra before t (मोऽनुस्वारः, 8.3.23).

morph.note: Causatives, curādi verbs and other derived stems form the perfect periphrastically: stem + -ām + the perfect of √अस् (आस). One verb serves both subjects, महासुरः (Caṇḍa) and मुण्डः.
अक्षि ‘eye’ at the end of a bahuvrīhi takes the stem -अक्ष, and the feminine adds -ई: भीमाक्षी.
The suffix -शस् makes distributive adverbs from numbers: सहस्रशः ‘in thousands’.

mantras.anvaya: महासुरः (चण्डः) महाभीमैः शरवर्षैः, मुण्डः च सहस्रशः क्षिप्तैः चक्रैः तां भीमाक्षीं छादयामास।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two subjects with their instruments — Caṇḍa with arrows, Muṇḍa with discuses — share the one verb छादयामास.
mantras.lit: The great asura covered that terrible-eyed one with most dreadful showers of arrows, and Muṇḍa with discuses hurled by the thousand.
mantras.tr: The great asura Caṇḍa buried the dread-eyed goddess under volleys of fearsome arrows, and Muṇḍa under discuses hurled by the thousand.
mantras.tr_note: ‘Caṇḍa’ is supplied: महासुरः continues the subject of 7.16.

comm.t: Both generals now attack together: Caṇḍa with arrows, Muṇḍa with discuses. ‘Covered’ (छादयामास) is the image of a storm of weapons that hides the target from sight.

flags.uncertain: महासुरः could also be read in apposition to मुण्डः (‘the great asura Muṇḍa covered her with arrows and discuses’). Since 7.16 makes Caṇḍa the attacker, he is taken as the subject of the first line.

Perfect of √भा, third plural: reduplication ब- (bh → b), the root’s ā dropped before -उः.

mantras.anvaya: तन्मुखं विशमानानि तानि अनेकानि चक्राणि, सुबहूनि अर्कबिम्बानि घनोदरं (विशमानानि) यथा, (तथा) बभुः।
mantras.anvaya_en: A simile: the discuses entering her mouth shone as very many suns (would) entering the belly of a cloud.
mantras.lit: Those many discuses, entering her mouth, shone like very many orbs of the sun (entering) the belly of a cloud.
mantras.tr: The countless discuses vanishing into her mouth shone like a multitude of suns sinking into the heart of a dark cloud.
mantras.tr_note: ‘Vanishing’ and ‘sinking’ render the participle ‘entering’, which the simile shares.

comm.t: Muṇḍa’s discuses do not wound her: they go into her mouth, as the weapons did in 7.13. The simile matches colour with colour — the bright discs are suns, the black mouth of Kālī (7.5) is a rain-cloud.

samasa.alt: Also read as a possessive: भैरवः नादः अस्याः अस्ति इति, ‘she whose roar is terrible’; the sense is the same.

samasa.vigraha: काल्याः करालं वक्त्रं कालीकरालवक्त्रम्; तस्य अन्तः (स्थिताः) दुर्दर्शाः दशनाः; तैः उज्ज्वला
samasa.type: tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, a karmadhāraya (करालं वक्त्रम्, दुर्दर्शाः दशनाः) and the adverb अन्तर्
samasa.literal: bright with the hard-to-behold teeth within Kālī’s dreadful mouth
samasa.sense: her gaping mouth shining with fearsome teeth
samasa.alt: Because काली and कराल meet without any sandhi, काली can also be taken as a separate nominative, the subject of the verse (‘Kālī, blazing with fearsome teeth within her dreadful mouth’). The Gita Press prints the whole as one compound, and it is kept so here; the meaning does not change.

morph.note: Perfect of √हस्: the reduplicated h becomes j (ज-हास), with vṛddhi in the third singular.
Neuter accusative used as an adverb, like द्रुतम् (7.6) and अतिभैरवम् (7.11).

mantras.anvaya: ततः कालीकरालवक्त्रान्तर्दुर्दर्शदशनोज्ज्वला भैरवनादिनी (सा) अतिरुषा भीमं जहास।
mantras.anvaya_en: Verb जहास with the adverbs अतिरुषा and भीमम्; the subject is given by two epithets.
mantras.lit: Then she who roars dreadfully, bright with the teeth hard to look at within Kālī’s dreadful mouth, laughed terribly in extreme fury.
mantras.tr: Then Kālī, roaring dreadfully, laughed a terrible laugh in her fury, the fearsome teeth in her gaping mouth flashing with light.
mantras.tr_note: The readable version makes Kālī the subject, as the alternative analysis of the compound allows; ‘flashing with light’ renders उज्ज्वला.

comm.t: Kālī laughs at the weapons that are meant to destroy her. Laughter and roar go together, and the mouth that swallowed the discuses now shines with its teeth.

Laughter in battle is a sign of the Goddess throughout the text: she laughs aloud in 2.32 (साट्टहासम्) and laughs as she drinks in 3.34 (जहास), and Śivadūtī’s laughter terrifies the asuras in 8.38 and 9.23. It is the fury of a power that cannot be harmed; the अट्टहास returns in 7.23.

samasa.sense: the Goddess’s lion-mount (सिंहस्योपरि, 7.3); महत् becomes महा- in such a compound, as in 3.32 (महासिंहं तं चकर्ष)

morph.note: उद् + स्था loses the s of the root (उत्थाय). The absolutive is usually intransitive (‘rising’); here the accusative महासिंहम् gives the place she rises onto: ‘rising onto the great lion’, i.e. mounting it.
Imperfect of the rudhādi root √छिद्, which inserts the nasal infix in its strong stem (छिनद्-/छिनत्). After the augment a the ch is doubled to cch (छे च, 6.1.73).
√धाव् is ubhayapada; here the ātmanepada imperfect (-त), while 7.21 has the parasmaipada अभ्यधावत्.

mantras.anvaya: देवी च महासिंहम् उत्थाय चण्डम् अधावत; अस्य केशेषु च गृहीत्वा तेन असिना शिरः अच्छिनत्।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two sentences: mounting the lion (absolutive उत्थाय with its object), she rushed at Caṇḍa (अधावत); and, seizing him by the hair, she cut off his head with that sword.
mantras.lit: And having risen onto the great lion, the Goddess rushed at Caṇḍa; and having seized him by the hair, she cut off his head with that sword.
mantras.tr: Mounting the great lion, the Goddess charged at Caṇḍa, seized him by the hair, and with that sword struck off his head.
mantras.tr_note: ‘Mounting’ renders उत्थाय with the accusative: literally ‘rising up onto’.

comm.t: Caṇḍa is killed exactly as Śumbha had ordered the Goddess to be treated: seized by the hair (केशेष्वाकृष्य, 6.23). देवी here is Kālī, the subject since 7.16; she charges on the lion that carried the Goddess in 7.3, and ‘that sword’ is the one she was born holding (असिपाशिनी, 7.6). Note on the text: the Gita Press digital file printed महासिं हं, with a space inside the word, which could be misread as ‘great sword’ plus a cry ‘haṃ’. Both witnesses (GRETIL, Freund) read महासिंहं as one word, and the text has been corrected accordingly (corrections.json, 7.20).
